findings.title: Webhook secret comparison is not constant-time and fails open when secret is unset
findings.body: The secret is compared with `!==` against `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If that env var is unset/empty and the header is missing, `req.headers[...]` is `undefined` and `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is `undefined`, so the check passes. The feature-flag check at line 19 partly guards this, but the handler itself does not require a configured secret. Also the comparison is timing-unsafe. Require a non-empty secret and use a constant-time comparison.

findings.title: Decryption with empty fallback key and unguarded JSON.parse
findings.body: `symmetricDecrypt` is called with `process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""`, and `JSON.parse` wraps the result. A bad key or malformed ciphertext throws an unhandled exception (500 with stack/no structured message) rather than a 400. Also `appointmentMetadata.slug` lookup uses the DB slug while the schema validation via `.parse` on line 31 throws a ZodError as an unhandled 500 for malformed bodies.

findings.title: Credential lookup by appId uses metadata slug but credential is keyed by app slug and type is unchecked
findings.body: The existing credential is looked up only by userId and appId, not by type. An app can have multiple credential types for one user (e.g. the same app slug with different types), so the update may overwrite the wrong credential row, or the create may duplicate one. Matching on `type` as well is needed to be safe.

findings.title: Minimum token schema uses computed keys that do not validate what it claims
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` creates a key literally named "ZodString"-like string, not a wildcard. The schema therefore does not enforce an expiry number nor allow arbitrary properties, so the minimal-schema branch validates only `access_token` and silently drops the intended validation. Downstream code (e.g. Google, Zoom) then receives tokens lacking the fields they need (refresh_token is also forced to a placeholder string 'refresh_token' on line 26 when missing, which would overwrite the stored refresh token with a bogus value).

findings.title: Placeholder refresh_token written into stored credentials
findings.body: When the refresh response has no refresh_token, the function sets it to the literal string "refresh_token" and this value is persisted (e.g. Google, Lark, Office365 write the parsed data back). The real refresh token is destroyed, so future refreshes will fail permanently. The fallback should preserve the existing refresh token instead.

findings.title: Refresh token and user data sent to an externally configured endpoint for every refresh
findings.body: When sync is enabled, the function POSTs the user id and app slug to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and returns that raw fetch Response as if it were a refresh result. The response is not checked for `ok`, and callers then treat it as a token response. A failing sync endpoint returns an error body that is parsed as tokens. The fetch also has no timeout and no auth header, so any caller reaching this path can be spoofed. Check response.ok and handle errors explicitly.

findings.title: Sync path skips the local refresh and returns a Response, changing callers' contract
findings.body: Callers such as Google use `res?.data`, Zoho and Office365 call `handleErrorsJson`/`.data` on the result, and Hubspot assigns `expiryDate` on it. The sync branch returns a fetch `Response` (no `.data`, no parsed JSON), while the normal branch returns an axios/googleapis result with `.data`. Mixed return types cause runtime undefined access in several services (e.g. Google `token.access_token` on a Response).

findings.title: Zoho CRM expiry date is hardcoded to one hour from now
findings.body: In refreshAccessToken the expiryDate is computed as `Date.now() + 60 * 60` (milliseconds, i.e. about one second) and the callback does the same. The token is treated as expired almost immediately, so every call triggers a refresh. The unit mismatch should be `* 1000` on expires_in.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh uses unhandled fetch with no response check and missing prisma import
findings.body: `prisma` is used at line 96 but is not imported in this file, so the module fails to compile or throws at runtime. Also `response.statusText !== "OK"` is an unreliable check (HTTP/2 has empty statusText) and the error is thrown before reading the Salesforce error body. Additionally the new token parse rejects responses lacking fields like `id`/`signature` that Salesforce omits on refresh, so refresh can fail for valid tokens.

findings.title: Removed error logging loses diagnostics for failed token parse
findings.body: The `console.error` branch logging the zod error and the Microsoft response was deleted. Now a failed parse silently falls through with `tokenResponse.success` false and the existing credentials are written back unchanged, so failures are invisible.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a string or undefined, not a boolean
findings.body: The expression `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` yields the env string value or undefined. It is used as a boolean in conditions, but the exported type is misleading and an empty-string env value is falsy while a non-empty one leaks the secret value into the constant. Use `!!` to coerce.

findings.title: Redirect URI hardcoded and no longer matches the callback's slug source
findings.body: The add handler now hardcodes `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback` while the callback still builds the URI from `appConfig.slug`. Changing the slug-based value to a literal is unnecessary churn and risks drift if the slug changes; it should remain `appConfig.slug` to stay consistent with the callback that must send an identical redirect_uri for the token exchange.

findings.title: isTokenValid logic inverted in Hubspot, Google-style check uses wrong comparison
findings.body: `(token.expiresIn || token.expiryDate) < Date.now()` treats an expired token as valid in the sense used by getToken and triggers refresh when the token is still valid, or vice versa; the expiry is also measured from expiresIn (a duration, not a timestamp). Expiry should compare expiryDate against Date.now().

findings.title: Callback expiry computed without multiplying by 1000 ms
findings.body: `Math.round(Date.now() + 60 * 60)` adds about one second, not one hour, to the current timestamp, so the stored expiryDate is effectively now and tokens are refreshed on every use.

findings.title: Duplicate and unsorted env entries
findings.body: CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME and CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET are inserted out of alphabetical order, and INTERCOM_SECRET was already duplicated before this change. Minor, but the list is used for cache keys and should stay deduplicated and sorted.

findings.title: Header name comment says lowercase but the default and lookup are case-sensitive
findings.body: The comment asks for a lowercase header name, but Next.js lowercases incoming header keys only; the webhook handler indexes req.headers with the env value directly, so a mixed-case configured name would never match. The code should lowercase the configured name or the docs should say so.

findings.title: No tests added for the new webhook or token refresh behaviour
findings.body: The PR adds a new authenticated endpoint that writes credentials, plus changes to refresh logic in about twenty services, with no tests. The PR checklist explicitly says tests were not added. At minimum the webhook auth, decryption failure, and sync-endpoint error paths need coverage.
